items.title: Colts signed OL Wanya Morris off the Cowboys’ practice squad.
items.text: Jalen Travis and Bernhard Raimann are both dealing with injuries, and other names on the Colts 53-man roster at tackle include Luke Tenuta, Charlie Heck, and Matt Goncalves (a guard last year) as they try to see out the end of this disastrous season. Morris will attempt to see it with them. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Micah Parsons (knee) is questionable for Green Bay’s Week 12 game against the Rams.
items.text: We have no doubts he’ll play — Rams EDGE Myles Garrett said he was able to give Parsons some tickets for the 27-year-old’s long-awaited return yesterday. But players returning from PUP and IR have frequently just gotten a questionable tag regardless of how likely they are to play. Parsons got in limited work in each of the three practices this week. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Josh Jacobs (thumb) is questionable for Green Bay’s Week 11 game against the Rams.
items.text: He got in limited work in each of Green Bay’s three practices this week, though some of them were “estimated” given the short week. Matt LaFleur said he was unlikely to play on Monday, so perhaps this is just a gamesmanship questionable. Obviously, if Jacobs does play, he’d be a suitable low-end RB2. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Ravens waived QB Kedon Slovis.
items.text: He’ll reportedly garner interest from the Arizona Cardinals for some reason. Slovis, 25, played for Arizona in the preseason and the Texans in the 2025 preseason. Over his three preseason stints he’s 86-of-126 for 816 yards, three touchdowns, and three interceptions while taking nine sacks. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh, asked about feeding Omarion Hampton more, said “in hindsight, we should have done that sooner.”
items.text: Many cases of fantasy managers who drafted Hampton in the first two rounds this past August nodding fervently at this news have been reported. Hampton had 15 touches last week and 23 against the Ravens in Week 10. With Justin Herbert (concussion protocol) uncertain for Week 12, it looks like Hampton will be a major part of the game plan yet again against the Patriots. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Browns designated RB Raheim Sanders (hip) to return from injured reserve.
items.text: His 21-day window will open today. Sanders probably won’t come back to a real role unless there are injuries ahead of him, but perhaps he’ll cut into Dylan Sampson’s No. 2 role and make both of them unrosterable. - Rivers McCown

items.title: Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said Ken Walker (ankle) will participate in practice Tuesday.
items.text: “I’m not anticipating a ton of work,” Reid said of Walker, who has missed two straight games and did not practice Monday ahead of the team’s Thanksgiving matchup against Buffalo. “Let’s see how does. He’s feeling pretty good.” If he practices today and Wednesday, Walker should be active for Thursday night. The Chiefs have committed to Walker as the team’s lead back despite Emmett Johnson putting up elite numbers in his absence. Johnson would be startable only in deeper fantasy leagues if Walker is good to go for Thursday. - Denny Carter

items.title: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports Greg Newsome (ankle) will miss 4-6 weeks.
items.text: Newsome will undergo surgery after sustaining a high ankle sprain in Week 11. His absence could be a blow to a Giants secondary that has played well in 2026, allowing the NFL’s 12th lowest drop back success rate and 11th lowest drop back EPA. Newsome through Week 11 had allowed the lowest EPA per target of any Giants cornerback. - Denny Carter

items.title: The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette’s Gerry Dulac reports DK Metcalf could face fines from the NFL following his Week 11 ejection.
items.text: Metcalf won’t be suspended for his repeated fights with Eagles defenders on Sunday but he could be fined for the behavior. Metcalf’s meltdown came after he had one catch for two yards in the first half. Among the most inefficient wide receivers in the game, Metcalf has had a disappointing 2026 campaign as the team’s No. 1 wideout. He’ll profile as a flex option in Week 12 against a Broncos defense allowing the fourth fewest fantasy points per target to boundary wideouts. - Denny Carter

items.title: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald would not say if Sam Darnold (oblique) would start in Week 12.
items.text: Darnold was able to return to practice on Monday ahead of the Seahawks’ Week 12 game against the division rival Niners. Macdonald suggested he wouldn’t make a call on a starting quarterback before Wednesday though. “I think before making any declarations with Sam, we’ll get through Wednesday, see how Wednesday goes,” Macdonald said. “So nothing official yet. He was able to train a little bit here, do some rehab here, he also was able to get away.
